modelPurpose: A valid starter model that demonstrates every required section and can be copied before replacing domain-specific content.

product.name: Template Product
product.description: A replaceable starter product model that conforms to the schema and demonstrates required structure.

lexicon.definition: A world-anchored obligation or capability the product must support, expressed as the KR title.
examples: Reserve an available book copy for pickup
Prepare a paid cafe order for customer pickup
Return an eligible delivered item and issue the correct refund

lexicon.definition: The canonical end-to-end path that fulfills one primary duty, expressed as the KR description.
examples: A member searches for a book, reserves a copy, and receives pickup details.

lexicon.definition: An atomic behavioral transition with preconditions, trigger, and observable postconditions.
examples: Given a copy is available, when a member reserves it, then one active hold is created.

lexicon.definition: A measurable indicator of user-experienced quality, such as latency, correctness, freshness, or recoverability.
A threshold target for a UX SLI that defines acceptable experience for a critical duty or journey.
examples: 99% of valid reservations confirm in under one second.

lexicon.definition: A concrete end-to-end execution example that demonstrates correct behavior for a duty journey.
examples: Successful reservation of one available library copy.

lexicon.definition: A concrete execution example that demonstrates forbidden, failed, misleading, or unacceptable behavior.
examples: Two members receive confirmation for the same physical copy.

lexicon.definition: A domain entity that exists or is meaningful in the real world and anchors the product architecture.
An architectural separation justified by real-world duration, externality, or human/physical delay.
examples: Kitchen preparation may be asynchronous because cooking takes real-world time.

lexicon.definition: A product law that must remain true across all valid states and transitions.
examples: One accepted return may issue at most one refund.

ambiguityPolicy.principle: The model must be internally decidable. If ambiguity remains, the model must name the missing external fact instead of hiding uncertainty in vague wording.
requiresClarificationWhen: A duty cannot be mapped to at least one real-world object or interaction.
A network boundary lacks a real-world latency or causality justification.
A trace can be interpreted as both golden and anti-golden.
A weakening or breaking update lacks explicit compatibility classification.
A journey completion criterion cannot be evaluated from observable state.

objects.name: Member
objects.definition: A person with a valid library account who may reserve materials.

objects.name: Physical Book Copy
objects.definition: A specific physical copy of a book located at a branch.

objects.name: Hold
objects.definition: A reservation that prevents a book copy from being reserved by another member.

interactions.name: Search book catalog
interactions.description: A member searches the catalog and sees availability.

expectedRealWorldDuration.explanation: Catalog search is a fast digital lookup.

interactions.name: Place hold on copy
interactions.description: A member reserves one specific available physical book copy.

expectedRealWorldDuration.explanation: Creating a hold is a fast state change that must prevent double booking.

invariants.name: Single active hold per copy
invariants.statement: A physical book copy may have at most one active hold at a time.
invariants.rationale: Two members cannot pick up the same physical object.

networkBoundaries.name: Hold creation consistency boundary
networkBoundaries.description: Availability check and hold creation must remain causally tight.
networkBoundaries.realWorldProcess: A member claims one physical copy that no other member can simultaneously claim.
networkBoundaries.causalityJustification: The real-world object is singular, so the system must synchronously prevent two active holds for one copy.
networkBoundaries.userVisibleImpact: The member immediately sees whether the reservation succeeded.
networkBoundaries.failureMode: Two members could receive confirmations for the same copy.

objectives.title: Make borrowing easy and reliable
objectives.description: Members can reserve available books without confusion or double booking.
objectives.successMeaning: A member can find an available copy, reserve it once, and understand pickup details.

duties.title: Reserve an available book copy for pickup
duties.intent: Allow a member to claim one available physical copy for pickup.
duties.scope: Covers search, selecting a copy, creating a hold, and showing confirmation.
nonGoals: Checking out the book at the counter.

okrMapping.keyResultTitle: Reserve an available book copy for pickup
okrMapping.keyResultDescription: A member searches for a book, selects an available copy, and receives pickup confirmation.

journeys.title: Reserve a library book for pickup
journeys.description: A member searches for a title, selects an available physical copy, reserves it, and receives pickup details.
journeys.purpose: Make a physical copy unavailable to others and available for this member.
journeys.trigger: Member searches for a book title.
preconditions: The member has an active account.
At least one matching book copy exists.
completionCriteria: An active hold exists for exactly one copy.
The selected copy is no longer generally available.
variants: If no copy is available, the member may join a waitlist.
failureBoundaries: If the last copy was just reserved, no duplicate hold is created.
nonGoals: Checkout at pickup is outside this journey.

timing.causalJustification: Search and hold creation are fast digital actions, and the physical copy can only be claimed by one member.

steps.title: Show copy availability
steps.given: A member has an active account and searches for a cataloged title.
steps.when: The member submits the search query.
steps.then: The system shows available physical copies.
thenAssertions: Availability is tied to copy state.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The member sees whether a copy is reservable.

steps.title: Create hold
steps.given: A selected physical book copy is available.
steps.when: The member selects reserve for pickup.
steps.then: The system creates exactly one active hold for that copy.
thenAssertions: No other active hold exists for the same copy.

stateTransitions.notes: The selected physical copy becomes reserved.
A new hold is created and becomes active.

steps.title: Show confirmation
steps.given: An active hold has been created.
steps.then: The system shows reservation ID, branch, and pickup deadline.
thenAssertions: Confirmation refers to the created hold.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The member knows where and when to pick up the book.

steps.title: Reject duplicate attempt
steps.given: The last available copy has already been reserved.
steps.when: Another member attempts to reserve it.
steps.then: The system does not create a duplicate hold and offers another path.
thenAssertions: No second active hold is created.
steps.expectedUserVisibleOutcome: The member sees that the copy is no longer available.

stateTransitions.notes: No hold is created for the unavailable copy.

slis.name: Reservation confirmation time
slis.description: Time from selecting reserve to seeing confirmation or clear failure.

slis.name: Duplicate reservation prevention
slis.description: Whether one physical copy has no more than one active hold.

slos.name: Confirm under one second
slos.consequenceOfViolation: Members may retry and lose trust in whether the hold exists.

slos.name: Prevent double reservation
slos.consequenceOfViolation: Two members can be promised the same physical book copy.

golden.title: Successful book reservation
golden.description: A member finds one available copy, reserves it, and sees pickup details.
golden.trigger: Member searches for a known title.

events.title: Search title
events.observedOutcome: The member can reserve the copy.

golden.finalState: One active hold exists and the member sees pickup details.
golden.classificationReason: The trace satisfies the duty and the single-hold invariant.

antiGolden.title: Double reservation for one copy
antiGolden.description: Two members receive confirmation for the same physical book copy.
antiGolden.scenario: Two members attempt to reserve the last copy concurrently.
antiGolden.finalState: The same copy has two active holds.
antiGolden.classificationReason: This violates the invariant that one physical copy may have at most one active hold.

updates.summary: Initial model for reserving an available physical book copy.
updates.reason: Establishes the first complete version of this product representation.
updates.rolloutPlan: Adopt as baseline after schema and semantic validation.
